bug_semantics: EVerest's OCPP 2.0.1 stack (libocpp ChargePoint::message_callback) deserializes untrusted CSMS JSON into ocpp::CiString<N>, whose default policy throws StringConversionException (a std::runtime_error) when a string exceeds the template bound. A CiString<255> field (or CustomData.vendorId) longer than 255 characters therefore throws during handle_message / from_json. At libocpp < 0.26.2 that exception is not caught on the v2 handle_message path, so the exception escapes the OCPP module and abort()s the EVerest process (availability DoS; CWE-392). OCPP 1.6 later caught the same conversion error; v2 did not until 0.26.2.
flaw_origin: The OCPP 2.0.1 inbound path was first written in libocpp 40b148b649ae4fe5192cbbac1cd35ab0863580ed (PR EVerest/libocpp#68, 2022-12-22) by Kai-Uwe Hermann: templated String/CiString with throw-on-oversize, from_json calling set(), generated types including CustomData.vendorId as CiString<255>, and v201 ChargePoint::message_callback with no try/catch around receive()/handle_message. Parent 6c36130ae5900d80e2de1caf7165d4c81b8b2eff has neither include/ocpp/common/string.hpp nor lib/ocpp/v201/charge_point.cpp. Later incomplete remediations (2a572cbb json::exception-only catch; 3283265 StringTooLarge::Throw plus receive()-only StringConversionException catch and Truncate on security-event logging) left handle_message uncovered. everest-core never authored those lines; it consumed libocpp as a dependency (OCPP201 module from 2023-01) and only later vendored already-patched v0.31.1.

reasoning: CVE-2025-59398 is a real, published DoS in libocpp's OCPP 2.0.1 message receiver: inbound JSON with a string over 255 characters is turned into CiString<255> under the default Throw policy and the resulting StringConversionException is not converted into a CALLERROR, so EVerest's OCPP201 module process dies. The GitHub advisory is an NVD import with withdrawn_at null; CVE.org remains PUBLISHED, so this is not FALSE_POSITIVE. The crash is not in everest-core's OCPP201.cpp (the reporter's line-505 guess is a reservation callback). It is in libocpp ChargePoint::message_callback, which everest-core ran as a pinned dependency. The smallest public first-write of that v201 uncaught deserialize path is libocpp 40b148b649ae4fe5192cbbac1cd35ab0863580ed: parent tree lacks the v201 ChargePoint and templated String/from_json files; PR #68 is a single commit so it cannot be decomposed further. The 1.6 CiString length throw is older (types_internal.cpp) but is a refactor source for String::set, not the v2 inbound handler this advisory's 0.26.2 fix changes. Subsequent commits added incomplete catches and renamed the throw to StringTooLarge::Throw; they are not the BIC. The sink-closing patch is libocpp fb391b4 (#1052) in v0.26.2; everest-core first consumed it on main in b8ab277 (#1153, v0.26.1 -> fb391b4). The CVE-linked everest-core SHA 253432ae only retags that already-fixed pin to v0.26.2 on the 2025.4 branch.
